languages.name: French
languages.notes: Source language. Uses vous (formal). Has article contraction variables (du/de l').

languages.name: English
languages.notes: No formal/informal distinction in pronouns.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.notes: Uses usted (formal). Varies by country (vosotros in ES, ustedes in LATAM).

languages.name: German
languages.notes: Uses Sie (formal). Compound words make translations longer.

languages.name: Italian
languages.notes: Uses Lei (formal). Has article contractions similar to French (dell'/del/dello).

languages.name: Portuguese
languages.notes: PT-PT uses o senhor/a senhora (formal). PT-BR uses você. Significant differences between variants.

languages.name: Dutch
languages.notes: Uses u (formal).

languages.name: Polish
languages.notes: Uses Pan/Pani (formal).

languages.name: Czech
languages.notes: Uses vy (formal).

languages.name: Slovak
languages.notes: Uses vy (formal).

languages.name: Hungarian
languages.notes: Uses Ön (formal). Agglutinative language.

languages.name: Romanian
languages.notes: Uses dumneavoastră (formal).

languages.name: Bulgarian
languages.notes: Uses Вие (formal). Cyrillic script.

languages.name: Croatian
languages.notes: Uses Vi (formal).

languages.name: Serbian
languages.notes: Can use Cyrillic or Latin script. Uses Vi (formal).

languages.name: Slovenian
languages.notes: Uses Vi (formal). Has dual grammatical number.

languages.name: Greek
languages.notes: Uses εσείς (formal). Greek script.

languages.name: Turkish
languages.notes: Uses siz (formal). Agglutinative language.

languages.name: Russian
languages.notes: Uses Вы (formal). Cyrillic script.

languages.name: Ukrainian
languages.notes: Uses Ви (formal). Cyrillic script.

languages.name: Danish
languages.notes: Uses De (formal) but informal is increasingly common.

languages.name: Swedish
languages.notes: Du-reform: informal du is standard. Ni (formal) is rarely used.

languages.name: Norwegian
languages.notes: Uses du (informal is standard). Bokmål variant.

languages.name: Finnish
languages.notes: Agglutinative. Te (formal) exists but sinä (informal) is common.

languages.name: Japanese
languages.notes: Uses desu/masu form (polite). CJK characters = shorter text length.

languages.name: Korean
languages.notes: Uses hapnida/haeyo form (polite). Hangul script.

languages.name: Chinese (Simplified)
languages.notes: Uses 您 nín (formal you). CJK characters = much shorter.

languages.name: Chinese (Traditional)
languages.notes: Traditional characters. Uses 您 (formal).

languages.name: Arabic
languages.notes: RTL script. Uses antum (formal). MSA for written communications.

languages.name: Hebrew
languages.notes: RTL script. Hebrew does not have a strong formal/informal distinction.

languages.name: Thai
languages.notes: Uses khrap/kha polite particles. Thai script, no spaces between words.

languages.name: Vietnamese
languages.notes: Uses bạn (neutral) or anh/chị (polite). Latin script with diacritics.

languages.name: Indonesian
languages.notes: Uses Anda (formal). Latin script.

languages.name: Malay
languages.notes: Uses anda (formal). Very similar to Indonesian.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.notes: Uses aap आप (formal). Devanagari script.

languages.name: Bengali
languages.notes: Uses apni আপনি (formal). Bengali script.

languages.name: Catalan
languages.notes: Uses vostè (formal). Has article contractions (l'/d'/n') similar to French.

languages.name: Basque
languages.notes: Uses zu (formal). Language isolate, agglutinative.

languages.name: Irish
languages.notes: Uses sibh (formal). Celtic language with initial mutations.

languages.name: Afrikaans
languages.notes: Uses u (formal). Germanic language, related to Dutch.

languages.name: Swahili
languages.notes: Bantu language. Noun class system affects agreement.

_note: This list will be refined once we see which languages appear in the actual CSV data. expected_length_ratio is relative to French (1.0).
